Why do so many VR games look like such crap?

There's really no excuse for it. It's not a hardware limitation either. If Star Citizen, Elite Dangerous, Skyrim, Descent Underground, Sublevel Zero, Borderlands, Dead Island, Project Cars, Assetto Corsa, Euro Trucker 2, Serious Sam 3, and Dying Light can run in VR and still look good, there's no excuse for this level of terrible graphics in other VR games aside from it just being shovelware crap. I've run all of those games I just mentioned in VR on a freaking 7970 at decent settings with a good framerate.

The Crytek Back to Dinosaur Island and Unreal Showdown realtime demos absolutely prove that there is zero reason for a game to look this bad just because it's VR on any 'VR Ready' system. If my old 7970 could run those then there's no excuse for the more powerful cards the HMD devices like Vive and Oculus CV1 require to be running at this level of awful and bland.

Blaming hardware limitations is a deflection, not an excuse. There's plenty of proof it's complete BS that this is as good as VR can do.

A shooter like this would be cool in VR, and it doesn't have to be Crysis 3 or anything, but there's no reason at all it should look this bad either.

I know VR can do far, far better than this because I've seen it and have even run it myself on lesser hardware that is actually below 'VR ready' standards. It's pretty bad when a lot of very early demos of the dev kit look better than your game does.

Because most (including this one) are indie games done by 1-2 people at most.

I'd like to see better looking VR games as well, but the limited installed base makes it difficult to convince studios to invest a lot into AAA experiences for VR.

I think for a while we're going to see more adaptations like Fallout 4 VR before getting really good experiences specifically tailored for VR.
